summary: Two corrections, each deleting a statement that was false. (1) Removed the hand-maintained `最后更新：YYYY-MM-DD` header line from all 8 documents under docs/ that carry one - docs/spec/operations/OPERATOR_CONTROL.md, docs/spec/strategy/STRATEGY_ECONOMICS.md, docs/spec/product/ASSET_ADMISSION.md, docs/intent/PROJECT_GOALS.md, docs/spec/strategy/LP_METRICS.md, docs/spec/product/WEB_CONSOLE.md, docs/spec/research/DATASET_AND_EVALUATION.md and docs/implement/TRACEABILITY.md. That set is exactly what `grep -rn '^最后更新：' docs/` returns, so my count agrees with the Manager's eight; one line was deleted per file and nothing else (git diff --numstat reports 0 insertions and 1 deletion in each). The `状态：` line above it, the blank line after it, the heading and every other character are unchanged. (2) Rewrote the amendment-layer paragraph of todo/WORKFLOW.md (now lines 99-111) so that it describes the four layers that exist - CONTRACT, SPEC, PROPHET, SUPERSEDE - instead of the retired INTENT layer, and so that its PASS and retry sentences hold for all four. Totals: 9 files changed, 11 insertions, 16 deletions (8 documents: 8 deletions; todo/WORKFLOW.md: 11 insertions, 8 deletions). No file was created, deleted or renamed, `git diff --check` is clean, and `python -m tools.workflow validate` reports OK in this worktree.
rationale: DEFECT 1. The deleted line had no checkable source of truth other than Git: a repo-wide search for `最后更新` finds it only in the 8 documents, in the A0006 amendment records that quote it, and in the controller's request for this amendment - nothing under tools/, tests/ or .github/ reads it, so it could only rot silently. The deletion is a deletion of one line per file, not an editorial pass: each document's heading, `状态：` line, blank line and section structure are byte-identical to the base (verified by reading the diff of all 8 files). The `date:` field in ADR front matter was deliberately not touched, since it records when a decision was taken rather than when a file was edited; no file under docs/spec/architecture/adr/ appears in the diff at all (14 ADRs carry such a field). One measured disagreement with the direction's justification is recorded in unresolved_questions rather than reproduced here. DEFECT 2. The old paragraph listed `CONTRACT`, `SPEC` and `INTENT`, and asserted that a PASS leaves the target tasks `PLANNED` and that a retry starts a fresh `Planner`. `AMENDMENT_LAYERS` is frozenset({CONTRACT, SPEC, PROPHET, SUPERSEDE}) (tools/workflow/core.py:36); `INTENT` appears nowhere in the controller's layer handling, so the paragraph was naming a layer that cannot be selected. The replacement was derived from the code the direction pointed at, branch by branch: (a) CONTRACT/SPEC text was kept because it is true - every non-PROPHET layer requires at least one target (core.py:1446-1447), its targets must be `PLANNED` (core.py:1452-1460), and at finish only the target contracts plus todo/config.yaml are writable, with docs/spec/ added for SPEC (core.py:1544-1546); (b) PROPHET refuses `--task` and is the only layer allowed an empty target set (core.py:1441-1445, 1486), it may write docs/intent/, docs/spec/, docs/implement/, README.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, todo/README.md, todo/WORKFLOW.md, a phase README.md and newly added task contracts, while a modified contract or any deletion is refused (core.py:493-520), and its config drift test frees only the two revisions and the tasks it adds (core.py:469-487, 1554-1568) - so the sentence 'it states Intent, restructures the plan and corrects collateral documents, may add tasks, and may change both revisions' says only what those branches permit; (c) SUPERSEDE targets must be `APPROVED` (core.py:1452-1460) and it may change only `superseded_by`, validated to name an existing task other than itself (core.py:684-697), plus the target contract text (core.py:460-461). The PASS sentence was replaced by 'fast-forwards the reviewed amendment into the clean invoking checkout without changing any target's status': the pass is a fast-forward-only merge of the reviewed branch (core.py:1703), and the config comparison forbids any target status change in every layer, so a CONTRACT or SPEC target is still `PLANNED`, a SUPERSEDE target still `APPROVED`, and a PROPHET change has no target. The retry sentence was replaced by 'uses `prepare-amendment-retry <id>` on the same layer', which is what the code does - the gate accepts CHANGES_REQUESTED or resolved BLOCKED, keeps `layer` and `task_ids`, and rebases on the retained candidate (core.py:1750-1778). The role name the old text carried was not replaced with another role name because the code is not consistent about it: the retry returns agent `planner` for every layer including PROPHET (core.py:1778), while the initial PROPHET author is the `prophet` agent (core.py:1495-1501); that is recorded as a question for the Owner instead of being described as if it were settled. Everything else in the paragraph was preserved verbatim: the status/attempt/evidence/commit/approval freeze sentence is true of all four layers, and the eight-target cap, the single-live-amendment rule and the unfinished-task gate are unchanged in code (core.py:1423-1433, 1448). No requirement, acceptance criterion or Must-not clause anywhere was weakened; no task contract, no todo/config.yaml, no ADR, no schema, no controller code and no test is in the diff.
unresolved_questions: Stale-date figure, recorded rather than reproduced, as the direction instructed. The direction says four of the eight stamped dates were already wrong because OPERATOR_CONTROL.md, STRATEGY_ECONOMICS.md, ASSET_ADMISSION.md and PROJECT_GOALS.md 'were modified on 2026-09-19'. Measured against Git (`git log -1 --format=%cs -- <path>`), only two are stale: docs/spec/strategy/STRATEGY_ECONOMICS.md (stamp 2026-09-14, last changed 2026-09-19 by c7a788d) and docs/intent/PROJECT_GOALS.md (stamp 2026-09-16, last changed 2026-09-19 by 9d6c1b1, previously c7a788d). docs/spec/operations/OPERATOR_CONTROL.md and docs/spec/product/ASSET_ADMISSION.md both still read 2026-09-14 and were last changed on 2026-09-14 by 24c0790, so their stamps matched their last edit; their 2026-09-19 mtimes are an artefact of `git worktree add` at 11:19:24, and the invoking checkout still shows 2026-09-14 17:41:43 for both. So six of the eight stamps were accurate at the moment of removal and two were stale, not four. The removal itself was carried out on all eight as directed; only the justification figure differs, and if the Owner wants the 'it rots' argument to rest on measured facts, the accurate statement is two stale and six accurate.

Retry author for a PROPHET change. `prepare_amendment_retry` returns agent `planner` for every layer (tools/workflow/core.py:1778), including PROPHET, while `prepare_amendment` returns the `prophet` agent for a PROPHET change (core.py:1495-1501) and the record's author file is named prophet-<attempt>.json (core.py:1577). The direction's premise that a retry starting a fresh `Planner` does not hold for PROPHET is therefore not what the code does today. Because the document could not safely assert either behaviour, the rewritten paragraph names no retry author and says only that the retry re-enters the same layer. Owner decision needed: should a PROPHET retry be returned to the prophet agent (a change under tools/workflow/, hence an explicit bootstrap act), or is the planner-labelled retry intended and the direction's premise the thing to drop?

The header status convention, which the direction asked to be recorded rather than decided. Every one of the eight documents keeps a hand-maintained `状态：...` line above the deleted date. It has the same three properties that made the date line false: it is prose, no command checks it (a search of tools/, tests/ and .github/ for `状态` returns nothing), and it asserts a state of confirmation that changes independently of the text around it. Recorded for the Owner to decide whether that convention should survive, be derived from something enforceable, or be dropped; nothing about it was changed here.

.claude/agents/planner.md lines 79-81 still carry the defect this amendment repaired in todo/WORKFLOW.md: they describe an amendment as targeting 'multiple still-`PLANNED` task contracts' within the '`CONTRACT`, `SPEC`, or `INTENT` layer'. The retired `INTENT` name therefore survives outside todo/WORKFLOW.md, and that paragraph is false for PROPHET (no target) and for SUPERSEDE (APPROVED targets) in exactly the way the rewritten paragraph was. `.claude/` is outside every role's scope and the direction forbade touching it, so it is unchanged; correcting it requires an explicit bootstrap act.

The paragraph immediately above the same code block in todo/WORKFLOW.md still opens 'When the Owner explicitly directs a planning change for one or more tasks that are still `PLANNED`', which describes neither PROPHET (targets no task) nor SUPERSEDE (targets APPROVED tasks). It was left untouched because the direction said not to change any other part of todo/WORKFLOW.md; the same sentence structure that required the layer list to be corrected also applies to it, so it is recorded for the Owner rather than silently fixed.

docs/intent/PROJECT_GOALS.md is the binding V1 goal document and its content changed here by one deleted line, yet `intent_revision` still reads v1-2026-09-19-research-universe-numeraire and `spec_revision` v1-2026-09-19-research-threats-and-strategy-extension (todo/config.yaml lines 5-6). The direction explicitly forbade editing todo/config.yaml, and the PROPHET layer freezes every config field except the two revisions and the tasks it adds (tools/workflow/core.py:469-487), so both revisions were left alone. A0006 raised the same question (whether a link-only repair ought to bump intent_revision) and left it open; if the Owner wants a PROPHET edit of Intent to move the revision pointer, the rule needs to be stated somewhere a future change can follow, since nothing in the repository derives or enforces it.
